As we wait for Flight 12 of Starship, I thought I’d share some of the images, sights and sounds around Starbase today. Nice views of the launch suite, another deluge system test, a walk around the Starfactory & views into the Gigabay which is well into construction.

So, what is coming up? After midnight tonight, expect both Booster 19 and Ship 39 to depart the production site for the launch pad and then stacking the ship onto the booster ahead of a planned Wet Dress Rehearsal (WDR) tomorrow.

Both the Ship and Booster already have the FTS installed and the ship is loaded with the payload (20 Starlink Simulators and 2 More with reaction wheels and cameras) so if all goes well with the WDR tomorrow, they wont need to de-stack and can go right into prep for Wednesday launch attempt, which is currently planned for 20 May at 5:30 PM CST.

So, the next 48 hours should have plenty of activity here at Starbase! Hoping for good luck for the Starship team!

Elon Musk shared major updates on Neuralink today.

Neuralink is building a direct interface between the human brain and AI. The technology has already helped people with severe paralysis use computers and phones again.

Musk says it could eventually help people walk by bypassing damaged areas of the spinal cord. Neuralink is also working toward restoring vision, even for people who no longer have functioning optic nerves or eyes.

Early restored vision may begin at low resolution before improving dramatically over time. Musk believes the technology could eventually enable vision beyond normal human capability.

He described restoring movement and sight as one of the most important breakthroughs imaginable for humanity.

Elon Musk predicts there could eventually be more intelligent robots on Earth than humans.

He believes the rise of advanced robotics and AI could lead to an era of “universal high income,” where automation dramatically increases productivity and abundance.

Musk also emphasized the importance of staying cautious and focused on robot safety as the technology rapidly advances.

The age of humanoid robots is starting to move from theory into reality.

Elon Musk says Tesla’s approach to full self-driving is built almost entirely around AI and vision.

Instead of relying heavily on radar or lidar, Tesla uses cameras and neural networks to drive in a way that more closely mirrors how humans navigate the world using vision and the brain.

Musk says the goal is for Tesla’s system to eventually become far safer than human drivers by a significant margin.

He also revealed that fully autonomous Tesla vehicles with no driver or safety monitor are already operating in three cities in Texas, with broader expansion across the US expected over time.

“It feels like the car is alive,” Musk said while describing the experience of using FSD.
